The full evidence set—young myopic woman with acute unilateral vision loss and metamorphopsia, posterior-pole yellow-white spots, quiet vitreous, SD-OCT focal EZ elevation with hyperreflective material, intact RPE/BM, and no CNV on SD-OCT/OCTA—matches MEWDS. Confidence is held at 0.7 pending FAF/FA/ICGA/ERG and serologic confirmation.

node-11.label: OCTA showed no choroidal neovascularization in the left eye

attrs.why: This subtype refinement of white dot syndrome is reinforced by the Radiologist's integrated analysis, which favors MEWDS as the leading white dot syndrome here. The shared demographic, clinical, and SD-OCT features and the absence of CNV support it, but as the confirmatory imaging and electrophysiology are still missing, confidence remains 0.7.

The Radiologist's integrated analysis favors MEWDS and offers no support for AZOOR, which typically lacks the transient posterior-pole yellow-white spots seen here. The SD-OCT ellipsoid-zone disruption keeps AZOOR marginally possible, so confidence remains 0.1 pending FAF/ERG.

The Radiologist's integrated analysis, combined with the absence of choroidal neovascularization on SD-OCT/OCTA, the lack of vitreous inflammation, and no hemorrhage on fundoscopy, argues against the typical MFC/PIC picture in this young myopic woman, so confidence remains low at 0.08.
